div.div: Each service slows for its own reason: pool CPU from alone to the full stack, GPU turns from the full stack to full stack + VLA, and two of the largest full-stack numbers were our bench and a logging bug, not the platform
All measured values on this page are illustrative measurements: round teaching numbers that keep the shape of each finding (class in constants.json). Pre-registered verdicts are in bold quotes.

SERVICE and symptom
alone -> full stack (-> + VLA)
CAUSE supported by evidence (confidence)
EXPERIMENT that showed it

CORRECTION kept visible
(first reading -> corrected)

The depth camera service, frame rate
30 Hz alone [camera_hz_alone, illustrative]; loses 5 Hz in the full stack [camera_full_stack_loss_hz, illustrative]

[CPU] Pool CPU load + the full stack's extra topic demand (fan-out); provisional.
GPU sharing alone costs 0 Hz with an idle pool [camera_gpu_only_loss_hz, illustrative].
Confidence: medium

One load per window: GPU minor; pool "undecided at dose"; fan-out a minor share (1 of 5 Hz [camera_fanout_loss_hz, illustrative]).
Weight arm: cpu.weight 100 -> 1000 [cpu_weight_default; weight_raised, illustrative]: verdict "split".

"The camera is GPU-bound" -> weakened: GPU load alone cost it no frames; GPU + pool load together not tested.
"nice on its threads tests priority" -> invalid test: each container is its own cgroup (note A3).

The object detector, frame time
100 -> 200 ms per frame [detector_frame_ms_solo_full, illustrative]

[CPU] alone -> full stack: run-queue wait is the largest added term, plus the same work running slower (medium-high).
[GPU] full stack -> + VLA: GPU time-slicing between processes (medium-high in a camera-plus-detector row; expected, not tested, in the full stack).

Inventory: per-frame wait / run / blocked split (page 03).
Counters: same instructions, more cycles (page 04).
Dose series: "dose explains"; the full stack placed on the curve is post-hoc (note B1).

"CPU changes full stack -> + VLA are within spread" -> withdrawn: with voice on in both, pool wait rises.
"SM contention" -> time-slicing (no MPS, no overlap; page 05).
"neither alone" -> the low end of a convex curve.

Voice chain (the speech recognizer -> the dialogue engine), transcript p50
600 -> 850 ms [transcript_latency_ms: alone, full, illustrative]

[BUG] A logging cost in the dialogue engine that grows with conversation history, on its asyncio thread: one INFO line per history item.
Confidence: high for alone -> full stack

Log filter in the full stack: context loop about 225 ms (my estimate from `ms_per_history_item` and `history_items`) -> 10 ms [context_build_ms_filtered, illustrative]; transcript p50 640 ms [transcript_latency_ms: full_filtered], near alone.
Not the platform: the largest voice number was our own software's logging loop, O(history) (note A4).

The interaction service, request accepted p50
2 -> 40 ms [interaction_accepted_ms: alone, probe_on_its_core, illustrative]

[BENCH] Mostly our measurement probe on the same reserved core: about 90 % of the rise (my estimate from `interaction_accepted_ms`: (40 − 5) ÷ (40 − 2) ≈ 0.92).
Confidence: high

Probe move to a pool core: accepted p50 5 ms [interaction_accepted_ms: probe_moved].
Predicted near alone: met; refutation rule not met.
"The platform is loaded, so the service's latency rises" -> about 90 % of the rise was our probe on the service's core (page 02).

The motor-control services, cycles for the same work
1.4× to 2× the alone cycles [cycles_growth_range, illustrative]

[CPU] Same work, more cycles (IPC loss), no run-queue wait. Moving their cluster-mates away removes about two thirds (f = 0.65 [cluster_move_recovered, illustrative]); path not isolated.
Confidence: medium

Counters: instructions per unit growth 0.0 [instr_growth, illustrative]; cycles +40 % to +100 % [cycles_growth_range].
Cluster move: "most (or less board traffic)", f above the 0.5 line [cluster_move_class_line, illustrative].
Predicted "part" (f below the line) -> measured above it but close to it. Read as "about two thirds", not a clean "most" (page 04).

The VLA, offered 5 Hz [vla_offered_hz, illustrative]
call 150 ms alone [vla_call_ms, illustrative]

[GPU] GPU-time-bound: it needs 0.6 s of GPU time per s, the stack leaves 0.4 [gpu_free_next_to_stack, illustrative] (my estimate from `vla_gpu_ms_per_call` and `vla_offered_hz`).
Confidence: medium

Budget (not a pre-registered test): 120 ms GPU work per call [vla_gpu_ms_per_call, illustrative]; the free time supports at most about 3.3 calls per s (my estimate from `gpu_free_next_to_stack` and `vla_gpu_ms_per_call`).
"GPU need = call time × rate" (0.75 s per s, my estimate from `vla_call_ms` and `vla_offered_hz`) -> no: a call contains CPU-side time; budget the GPU time per call (note C1).

Corrections not tied to one service: "A low SM issue rate means free room" -> about half the kernel time (0.5 [kernel_time_sms_full_share, illustrative]) already fills the SMs on some resource, by launch configuration (theoretical; note B2). "More GPU compute would not help" -> multi-wave kernels would run in fewer waves on more SMs (expectation, not measured). "The vision encoder is several times slower than predicted" -> the prediction used the bandwidth form, 6 ms [vision_pred_bandwidth_form_ms, illustrative], on a board where vision is compute-bound; the compute form gives 20–30 ms [vision_compute_form_ms, illustrative] (note B4).

Legend
Cause fill + tag: blue [CPU] = shared CPU pool / caches; green [GPU] = GPU time-slicing; teal = both (one per step); amber [BENCH] / [BUG] = our bench or our software, not the platform.
Purple dashed box = a correction: the first reading and what replaced it.
Bold quoted verdicts = pre-registered classes, unchanged.
Load levels: alone = one service; full stack = every module on, about 40 services [stack_services, illustrative]; + VLA = full stack plus a VLA (vision-language-action model) at its offered rate.

Sources. Every number is loaded from ../constants.json by spec01.py; its key is in brackets. Notes A0 (diagnosis map, corrections table), A1–A5, B1–B4, C1. Probe rates in the full stack are lower bounds; probe latencies are upper bounds (notes A1, A5).
Illustrative (round teaching numbers that keep the shape of a finding; not measurements): camera_hz_alone, camera_full_stack_loss_hz, camera_gpu_only_loss_hz, camera_fanout_loss_hz, weight_raised, detector_frame_ms_solo_full, transcript_latency_ms, ms_per_history_item, history_items, context_build_ms_filtered, interaction_accepted_ms, cycles_growth_range, cluster_move_recovered, instr_growth, cluster_move_class_line, vla_offered_hz, vla_call_ms, gpu_free_next_to_stack, vla_gpu_ms_per_call, kernel_time_sms_full_share, vision_pred_bandwidth_form_ms, vision_compute_form_ms, stack_services.
Public: cpu_weight_default = https://docs.kernel.org/admin-guide/cgroup-v2.html (cpu.weight).
